title: Fresh-seed review (30-33) of c42's held-out arena sizes: same result, 80^2 coexists on 4/4 and 40^2 on 1/4; at 40^2 predator droplets vanish for single counts in boom-bust cycles and reappear, which is what fails two of the three runs
summary: Ran the claimed world unchanged with the claim's drive.py on fresh seeds 30-33 at 40^2 and 80^2 (T=12000, counts every 100 t) and applied the stated rule (predators present at every count from t=6000, prey at >= 50% of those counts; rule.py). 80^2: 4/4 coexist (prey present at 98-100% of late counts, 6-12 predator droplets at the end). 40^2: 1/4 (seed 30, prey 57%); seeds 31 and 33 fail only because predator droplets are absent at 1 of 61 late counts (pred present 0.98) and then return; seed 32 loses its last predator droplet at t=11800. ho40_s33.png shows the small arena's boom-bust: predator mass peaks and crashes about every 2000 t and the droplet count touches 0 at t~8300 before predators re-form. labkit pack at 80^2 seed 30 (120 frames, --lineage-k 5): prey 5 and predator 9 persistent splits, both species present at the end.

observations.X: heldout_table.txt: 80^2 4/4 coexist, 40^2 1/4 on seeds 30-33 (prediction >= 3/4 and <= 2/4 both met again); ho80_s30.png, ho40_s33.png

seeds_run.result: 80^2 coexist; 40^2 not (pred absent at 1 count, t~8300, then return)

verdicts.limitation: The every-count rule is brittle at 40^2: 2 of 3 failures are a single count without a predator droplet in a boom-bust cycle, after which predators re-form from dilute material, so 'loses coexistence' there means transient absence, not extinction. Counts use a 0.5 threshold on each channel. I did not run other sizes.
